summary: RFCs 4328 and 7139 give RSVP-TE signaling extensions for controlling Optical Transport Network features, but they do not cover the additional ODU containers defined in G.Sup43. This informational document adds the signaling needed for those extra signal types.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7963 adds RSVP-TE signal types for three ODU containers that earlier signaling specifications did not cover. Each type has a registered number carried in traffic parameters.

questions: what signal types does rsvp-te support for otn
which odu signal types does rfc 7963 add
subtitle: Three added signal types identify additional ODU containers in RSVP-TE.

tldr.problem: Earlier RSVP-TE signaling specifications did not define signal types for ODU1e, ODU3e1, and ODU3e2 containers described in G.Sup43.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7963 defines three Signal Type values carried in OTN-TDM SENDER_TSPEC and FLOWSPEC traffic parameters: 23 for ODU1e, 26 for ODU3e1, and 27 for ODU3e2.
tldr.outcome: The signal types are registered in the GMPLS OTN Signal Type subregistry. The RFC notes that these container formats do not guarantee data-plane interoperability.

today: RFC 7963 is an Informational RFC that registers three additional OTN signal types for RSVP-TE. The document states that these data-plane formats do not guarantee interoperability.

sections.title: The Missing ODU Signal Types
sections.content: RFCs 4328 and 7139 provide RSVP-TE signaling extensions for Optical Transport Networks. RFC 7139 did not specify Signal Types for ODU1e, ODU3e1, and ODU3e2 containers defined in G.Sup43. RFC 7963 adds those missing types.
sections.plainLanguage: Earlier signaling rules left out three ODU container types. This RFC adds names and numbers for those types.

sections.title: The Registered Values
sections.content: The three registered values are 23 for ODU1e, 26 for ODU3e1, and 27 for ODU3e2. They are carried in the Signal Type field of the OTN-TDM SENDER_TSPEC and OTN-TDM FLOWSPEC traffic parameters defined by RFC 7139.
sections.plainLanguage: Each added container type has a number: 23, 26, or 27. RSVP-TE carries that number in its OTN traffic parameters.

sections.title: Interoperability and Security
sections.content: The document describes these containers as non-standard data-plane frame formats that are among approaches used within a network to transport 10GBASE-R signals. G.Sup43 does not guarantee data-plane interoperability for them. RFC 7963 introduces no additional security issues beyond those identified in RFC 7139.
sections.plainLanguage: The new signal numbers identify formats, but the RFC warns they do not guarantee that different equipment will interoperate. It adds no new security issues beyond RFC 7139.
